corrections.before:
Original calendar-year [2023](https://www.operationaccess.org/s/2023Form990.pdf), [2024](https://www.operationaccess.org/s/2024Form990.pdf) and [2025](https://www.operationaccess.org/s/2025Form990.pdf) returns report full-recipient expenses of $2,658,742, $2,678,152 and $2,261,505; their mean is $2,532,800. No direct fundraising-event, gaming or inventory cost addback was identified in Part VIII. These comparable tax-return totals exclude donated services but are not identical to cash expense. The [2025 audit](https://www.operationaccess.org/s/2025-Audited-Financial-Statements.pdf) records $22,876,888 including $20,530,000 of waived-charge clinical valuation and $89,922 of other in-kind support. Removing both gives $2,256,966 cash-like expense, about $1,476 per service; the remaining $4,539 difference from the tax total is not an event addback. Hospital charges are not incremental resources or health.

The conditional beta central is 0.531 California QALYs per $100,000 ordinary gift, or $1.88 million per ten QALYs. It assumes half the nominal mixed activity is additional, costs every donated dollar, and discounts repeat care, later equivalent treatment and harm. The observed aggregate patient conversion changes the alpha central only slightly. Five added slots raises the price to $12.56 million; rapid alternative care to $20.57 million; favorable joint judgments give $452,000. Null and harm scenarios remain explicit. None is a confidence interval.

Including $369,105 of modeled gross associated clinical, patient and downstream resources gives $6.95 million per ten QALYs. These allowances apply to all nominal activity, including activity not caused by the gift, so this is not a net societal cost-effectiveness estimate. Diagnosis shares and prospective cash unit costs remain judgments.

corrections.before:
The [2025 Form 990](https://www.operationaccess.org/s/2025Form990.pdf), page 2, reports 1,529 services to 1,130 unduplicated residents. The [annual report](https://www.operationaccess.org/s/Operation-Access-Annual-Report-2025.pdf) splits those services across ten specialties, records 627 people who volunteered that year, and reports a 72-day median wait to a specialty appointment—not necessarily definitive treatment or days of delay prevented. Its approximately 1,000-person network is a roster, not the same volunteer count. Services rose 15.8% from 2024; reported referrals rose 28%, but neither gives available slots for a new donor. Patient-reported improvement lacks an untreated comparator and cannot become QALYs directly.

Beta replaces the old repeat-service priors with 1,529/1,130 across a disjoint diagnosis ledger. Applying that aggregate ratio uniformly to marginal cases is a judgment. Diagnosis-specific people, baseline severity, treatment completion, validated utility, adverse events and alternative-care waits are still needed. An annual-report story requiring two operations illustrates why a procedure is not automatically a new beneficiary.

Patient-reported improvement lacks an untreated comparator and cannot become QALYs directly.

Beta replaces the old repeat-service priors with 1,529/1,130 across a disjoint diagnosis ledger. Applying that aggregate ratio uniformly to marginal cases is a judgment. Diagnosis-specific people, baseline severity, treatment completion, validated utility, adverse events and alternative-care waits are still needed. An annual-report story requiring two operations illustrates why a procedure is not automatically a new beneficiary. The 1,130 count is verified as an original filed organizational report, not as independently audited patient-level data. Using one aggregate ratio and mutually exclusive diagnosis allocations enforces arithmetic nonoverlap, but does not demonstrate that the marginal clinical mix has the same repeat-care pattern.
corrections.reason: Avoid overstating verification of source-reported unique patients.

corrections.before:
The [CMSP May 2025 minutes](https://cmspcounties.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/II_Correspondence.pdf), pages 2 and 14, record refusal of renewed funding after the five-year $5.7M grant. The board questioned expansion reach, rising per-person costs and changing public coverage. OA reported stronger referrals and restructured staffing. This is a genuine adverse funder assessment—not proof of no clinical benefit, and not proof a new gift restores lost care.

The [audited year-end accounts](https://www.operationaccess.org/s/2025-Audited-Financial-Statements.pdf) show cash down $246,920 but total net assets up $177,249: receivables and restricted support changed. There were $913,650 restricted net assets and $2,531,766 financial assets available within twelve months; OA reported 16 months of operating cash against an eight-month target. These are December 2025 balances, not current bank balances. The [2025 budget-versus-actual statement](https://www.operationaccess.org/s/2025OperationAccessFinancialStatements.pdf) reports a $222,752 operating deficit before future-pledge timing adjustments; it is not the GAAP surplus or cashflow. The [2026 budget](https://www.operationaccess.org/s/2026Budget-8pz4.pdf) plans $1.9M revenue and expense after restructuring, including $1.628M personnel. Replacement donations and reserves mean grant loss cannot be equated with present funding room.

[DHCS current rules](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/medi-cal/updates/medi-cal-changes/) freeze new full-scope enrollment for some adults from January 2026, while existing eligible enrollees can retain coverage by renewal and exceptions remain. Later scheduled changes are not already realized OA demand. Current English intake wording and OA's earlier bridge-care description differ; publicly eligible but unenrolled patients may obtain care later. We retain a transparent f=0.5 judgment, test 0.1 and zero, and do not claim a verified unmet gift offer. The next decisive evidence is funded versus unfunded approved cases, current slots, enrollment alternatives and 2026 unrestricted commitments.

Current English intake wording and OA's earlier bridge-care description differ; publicly eligible but unenrolled patients may obtain care later. We retain a transparent f=0.5 judgment, test 0.1 and zero, and do not claim a verified unmet gift offer. The next decisive evidence is funded versus unfunded approved cases, current slots, enrollment alternatives and 2026 unrestricted commitments. The CMSP minutes quantify the expansion concern: 91% of grant-period people served came from the original four counties and 9% from the eighteen expansion counties. This describes the grant evaluation, not California-wide clinical ineffectiveness. Current English intake explicitly says uninsured and ineligible for full-scope Medi-Cal, Medicare or CMSP; the Spanish version says uninsured without the same eligibility qualification. That inconsistency and historical bridge-care language require clarification before assuming all current participants are excluded from public alternatives.
corrections.reason: Make the adverse funder evidence and intake inconsistency precise.

Symptom Q_j=P_j*[success_j*utility_j*(1+discount)^(-delay_j)*F(catchup_j+loss_j+mortality_j+ln(1+discount),horizon_j)-harm_j]. For CRC let z(t)=delta_hazard*exp(-catchup*latency)*F(catchup,min(max(t-latency,0),active_years)); Δsurvival(t)=exp(-baseline_mortality*t)*(exp(z(t))-1). CRC Q=P_crc*[linkage*surviving_utility*(1+discount)^(-delay)*integral_0^H Δsurvival(t)*(1+discount)^(-t)dt - harm]. Full exact parameter vectors and scenario overrides are below. Numeric reproduction uses existing lib/oa-portfolio-model.mjs and lib/oa-portfolio-foundation.mjs; its regions.us.q equals CA here solely because eligibility was independently verified. The modeled service and patient equivalents represent completed care at the procedure date. The pre-procedure delay is discounted financially in time; no separate survival/catch-up attrition before completion is applied because it is assumed included in additional completed activity. If nominal activity instead means referrals, an additional completion/dropout factor is required. Procedural harm is conservatively charged without a favorable delay discount.
corrections.reason: Clarify time origin and completion assumption; no implicit guaranteed conversion of referrals.
